parsed.explanation: Section 379 criminalises female presentation by men in public with up to three months' imprisonment — a universal exposure for an outed trans woman, independent of any private conduct. Though the parallel 'unnatural offense' statute is documented unenforced (2018–2022), security forces are reported across those same five years to harass, arrest, detain, torture and beat LGBTQI+ persons: state-perpetrated, patterned, with impunity — no hate-crime or anti-discrimination law, a raided and shuttered support NGO, an official call for detention-until-procreation, and mass flight of openly LGBTQ citizens. Entry/document rules and care access are undocumented, not safe. No death penalty appears. The combination of a public-reach dress offence, documented custodial abuse by state actors, and hostile official framing places this in High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No data on passport markers, visa screening or border questioning of trans travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: Any document-presentation mismatch would feed directly into Section 379 exposure and security-force discretion, but the dossier establishes no specific border procedure either way.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Security forces reported 2018–2022 to arrest, detain, torture and beat LGBTQI+ persons; Section 379 supplies a public-presentation offence carrying up to three months' imprisonment; a 2017 minister called for detention until procreation.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented remedy: no hate-crime or anti-discrimination law; conduct-provision non-enforcement reported but no protection from detention itself.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An outed visitor entering custody meets documented state-perpetrated abuse with no oversight; foreign nationality offers no documented safeguard.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational variation documented; the dress and conduct provisions apply nationwide, so no safer region exists.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Nationwide uniformity means the exposure travels with the visitor throughout the country rather than being avoidable by itinerary choice.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No information on gender-affirming care, prescriptions or emergency-care refusal.
care_services.interaction: An injury or illness could reveal trans status to a system the dossier shows as hostile to LGBTQI+ people, but no specific care denial is sourced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official hostility documented: 2017 ministerial order-to-arrest statement, 2010 head-of-state denigration, constitutional same-sex marriage ban, NGO Act used to close a rights group, most openly LGBTQ citizens fled 'actively hostile' government rhetoric.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: This framing licenses security-force discretion the dossier shows being exercised, raising both outing probability and post-outing severity for a visibly gender-nonconforming visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No provision addresses accompanying minors; a parent's visible nonconformity would expose the family to the same Section 379 and security-force discretion.
minors_guardians.interaction: Hostile official framing and no child- or family-specific safeguard mean the minor inherits the guardian's exposure with no documented mitigation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 'Widespread' societal discrimination (2011, continued in later reporting), no support organisations, no legal recourse, documented security-force abuse — public outing risks both private hostility and state mistreatment.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None documented; no hate-crime statute, no functioning complaint mechanism shown.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Calling police would route the visitor into the actor the dossier identifies as an abuser rather than a protector.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime law; NGO space closed; oversight absent. Unknowns: Section 379 enforcement record, border/document practice, care access, fate of the 2017 detention order — none resolve toward safety.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Only the reported non-enforcement of the conduct provision (2018–2022), which does not extend to Section 379 or to security-force conduct.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin-data extrapolation: criminalisation, hostile governance and zero documented relief imply illusory remedies, per rule 13.

anchor_checks.comparison: Saruth combines entry detention, facility abuse, delayed courts and a faint capital echo. This dossier matches the state-perpetrated custody abuse and illusory remedies, and adds a public-reach dress offence, but lacks a documented border detention regime and any capital provision — so it sits slightly above 0.15-B.

Ostravia documents birth-sex prison placement, cross-dressing arrests in buildings and slow remedies, rated 0.25. This dossier's abuse is worse — torture by security forces is documented as a multi-year pattern with zero recourse — so it rates materially below 0.25-C.

Karthovia's police stop, interview and release without charge, with detention 'rarely becoming imprisonment', is friction plus humiliation. Here a criminal dress statute reaches public presentation and state forces are documented torturing detainees: clearly more severe, so this rating sits well below 0.35-B.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is uniform nationwide: a criminal statute that fires on appearance alone in public, an unenforced-but-retained conduct statute, and security forces documented across five consecutive years harassing, arresting, detaining, torturing and beating LGBTQI+ people. Layer on official detention rhetoric, a constitutional ban, an NGO Act that shut the only support group, widespread societal stigma, and no hate-crime or anti-discrimination law, and the traveller who is outed faces custodial abuse by the state itself with no remedy anywhere in the record. Non-enforcement of the conduct provision is the sole documented positive and does not shield against Section 379 or security-force discretion. Undocumented border, document and care rules are open questions, not safety; thin-data extrapolation from hostile governance points the same way.
